occasion: Any act is about to run in a session where nothing has listed a set. A bulk delete is not distinguishable before it runs without its name (Theorem 3), so the listing is owed before the first act; the removal itself is observed afterwards by U20, with the pre-image retained.

occasion: the run is ending after delegated work returned and before any returned artifact was read
costly: end the run by inheriting delegated work without inspecting what came back
guard: read a returned artifact after dispatch and before stopping
subject: session_id
deny_reason: ending after delegated work with no artifact read on record; use Read to inspect what returned before accepting it
_fixture_note: terminal clause: fixtures validate discharged_by, since the fingerprint is always
_note: Admission test: a delegated result is inherited as finished work by default. If nobody inspects it, later work is built on an unverified artifact and the missing observation cannot be reconstructed after the session ends; healing requires discarding the inherited result and restarting the work, path (3). The verdict row warns that a broad Read/Glob/Grep discharge can license one unit with activity about another. Tool-name events expose no shared unit or artifact operand, so an extractor would abstain rather than protect; this clause tightens the observable guard to an actual Read and activates only after dispatch. The remaining session-level approximation is admitted only if the frozen-corpus measurement reports no candidate false positives and its terminal firing rate stays below HIGH_INTERRUPT.

occasion: the act printed a passing report datum, and that PASS may later be cited as licensing evidence
costly: accepting a checker PASS that has never demonstrated it can reject an invalid or absent input
guard: run this same checker under a planted fault and see it FAIL: a failing report from the checker is the observation
subject: session_id
deny_reason: a checker reported PASS and this same checker has not been seen FAILING this session; run it under a planted fault so its failing report is observed, before citing the PASS
_fixture_note: The guard is the effect `report_fail` on a PostToolUse Bash record keyed by the checker; a can-fail cell that swallows the failure into its own PASS is not an observation Keel can make, so running the checker under the fault directly is what pays it.
_note: Individual admission decision: a checker that accepts missing or invalid input produces the same green result as a sound checker, so doing nothing preserves a false licensing fact and downstream work consumes the opportunity to distinguish them. Recovery requires reversing the accepted PASS, planting or removing input, and replaying the checker decision path (restart path 3). The occasion is narrowed to explicit pytest/unittest runners and named *check*/verify Python or shell scripts. Each PostToolUse `report_pass` record activates the clause and records the normalized checker command as its own obligation; only a PostToolUse `report_fail` record for the equal key discharges it. 2026-09-03: this sentence said `PreToolUse` activation and a `nonzero` discharge, which the shipped activated_by/discharged_by contradict -- both are `{kind: effect, ...}` on PostToolUse, and the `nonzero` predicate kind no longer exists. Corrected to the shipped guard. Admit only if the frozen corpus reports candidate_fp=0 and TABLE_SUM remains below 20 per 1000. 2026-08-20: the command-word class excludes = and quote characters. It was [^\s;&|]*, which a shell VARIABLE ASSIGNMENT satisfies -- F=plugin/makoto/checks/writeThrashRevert.py contains 'check' and ends .py, so it both activated the clause and became the key, and nothing can discharge a row that names no runnable checker. Measured in one live session: 114 demand rows, 19 of them keyed on a token containing =, over 18 distinct never-dischargeable subjects. A genuine invocation never carries = inside the program token, and 'export PYTHONPATH=/x; python3 -m pytest tests/' still keys off its second segment. See tests/test_c08_activation.py.

occasion: the act printed a process listing that contains a segment of its own command -- the checker appeared in its own result, by whatever program
costly: count or trust a grep-shaped process match without excluding the observer identity
guard: produce a listing that excludes the observer: the output holds live pids and none of the act's own command text
subject: session_id
deny_reason: a process listing contained its own checker; before the next act, produce a listing that excludes the observer (pids present, the act's own command text absent) so a match is not the observer
_note: Admission test: a checker included in its own observation can create a stable false-positive process count. That apparent presence is then used as fact, and repeated checks reproduce the same observer contamination; doing nothing never reveals the absent target. Recovery requires interrupting the accepted result and rerunning from a correctly separated observer, effectively restarting the decision path (3). The verdict's broad pgrep/pkill/killall branch is narrowed away because it does not require a grep process in a ps pipeline and would interrupt ordinary process operations unrelated to self-inclusion. The remaining fingerprint names the concrete self-match surface, while the guard requires an identity-bearing inverted filter rather than a name-only grep trick. Re-covered: both sides are effects read off the listing itself, so the observer's presence is a datum, not a pipe shape.

occasion: the trace is about to present a plan for adoption
costly: adopt a plan built on nothing read
guard: read something first, so the plan describes this repository and not a remembered one
subject: session_id
deny_reason: present a plan with no read, glob or grep on record; a plan is followed by default, so a plan built on assumption defines the whole path before anything is checked
_note: Measured hole: 29 ExitPlanMode calls in one session, zero clauses. A plan is the perfect asymmetry -- it defines the path and its end, and nobody decides to follow it.

occasion: the trace is about to present a plan whose ambiguities were settled by guessing
costly: adopt a plan built on a guessed reading of the request
guard: ask one question about the ambiguity before the plan is fixed
subject: session_id
deny_reason: present a plan with no question asked this session; reading files resolves what the repository is, never what was wanted, and a plan is followed by default
_note: P01 guards the same occasion and accepts Read/Glob/Grep as discharge, which answers a different question: reading establishes what the repository IS, not what was ASKED FOR. A plan can therefore be adopted having read forty files and asked nothing, and P01 counts it discharged. The two failure modes are independent -- a plan grounded in the tree can still be a plan for the wrong task -- so this is a separate clause rather than a widened P01. Against the admission test: left alone, a plan built on a guessed reading is FOLLOWED, because a plan's default is adoption and nothing in the run re-opens the interpretation. The state it leaves is work completed under the wrong goal, and that heals only by throwing the session away and starting over -- path (3), an ACTION, and the most expensive one. Its interruption cost is bounded by the occasion: ExitPlanMode is rare per session and one question discharges it for the whole session.

occasion: HEAD moved to a commit that already existed -- a switch or checkout, through whatever program
costly: switch or check out a git ref
guard: know the ref: a quiet act that prints the ref name or commit id the ref snapshot holds (`git rev-parse --verify REF`, `git branch`, `git show-ref`, or any listing of refs), or Read Keel's `observed.json`, which carries the refs
subject: session_id
deny_reason: HEAD moved to a ref nothing in this session observed; print the ref (`git rev-parse --verify REF`, `git branch`, `git show-ref`) before the next act
_natural_guard: Creating a ref is discharged by work someone actually does: `git checkout -B REF origin/main` is how a session makes the branch it later returns to, and creation is the strongest possible proof the ref exists. Measured on the frozen corpus: the sole U09 denial checked out `claude/gyroscope-terminal-clauses`, a branch the same session had created 12 calls earlier with `git checkout -B` -- the guard was already run, under a name the old discharged_by refused to see. `git rev-parse --verify` remains the explicit probe for refs the session did not make.

occasion: the act printed a null datum, or nothing at all while reading a structured file -- through whatever program
costly: traverse structured JSON data
guard: look at the structure first: a query on the same file that prints a non-null JSON datum (`jq 'keys'`, `jq 'type'`, `jq -e 'has(...)'`), or Read the file
deny_reason: a traversal of structured data produced null; look at the structure before the next act: print a non-null JSON datum from the file (`jq 'keys'`, `jq 'type'`), or Read the file
_natural_guard: The old guard demanded specifically `jq -e` with a type/has assertion -- a ritual observed 0 times in 2152 real Bash calls. The observation people actually make before traversing a JSON file is `jq 'keys'` or `jq 'type'` on it: measured on the frozen corpus, the session ran `jq 'keys' FILE` before every per-file traversal chain (e.g. call 2100 `jq 'keys' calibration_preregistered.json` precedes 2104 `jq 'del(.tasks)'` on the same file). That look is the guard -- it answers the same question (what shape is this document) and is discharged by work that is already part of the job. `jq -e` still discharges. COMPOSED over the host surface, the same move U12 and U19 took to Grep: reading the file IS looking at its structure, and `Read` is a CLOSED host enum, so naming it retires a vocabulary instead of widening one -- a `jq`-only guard is monotone in vocabulary (Coverings.v Thm 5) and is defeated by inspecting the file any other way. The subject had to move with it: a Read carries its file in `tool_input.file_path`, not in a command, so with a single-field subject the composed guard would key to "" and discharge nothing.

occasion: a file that existed before the act has different content after it -- rewritten by whatever program

_natural_guard: The old guard demanded `cmp` or a checksum comparison BEFORE the rewrite -- observed 0 times in 2152 real Bash calls, an added obligation: the rewrite landed identically whether or not anyone ran it. The act that actually reverses a blind in-place rewrite is locating the text first, and that is what sessions do: grep/rg appear 504 times in the frozen corpus, the first at call 8, before every `sed -i`. This mirrors U12, which already discharges patch application on rg/grep -- the same act shape gets the same natural guard. cmp/sha256sum remain as the explicit byte-level form.
